FOR campaign/the-fetch -- ROUND 4 RED, and it produced the single most legible piece of evidence in this whole sequence. Two failures, both from campaigns that landed tonight, and the second one shows the behaviour change in reader-visible prose.

    turn_budget::the_route_memo_survives_between_waits
      "denominator: the first wait ran no route searches at all, so this seed's
       belief fold never reaches the memo and the invariance below would be vacuous"

    the_warrant::every_gloss_and_its_first_day_survives_the_flip
      seed 23, entity 10597402111491375104, glosses vs the frozen before-image:

        frozen:  (363003, "went down to the river it knew (thirst)")
        actual:  (381584, "drifted homeward, missing its people (belonging)")

THE THIRST ERRAND IS GONE. The creature no longer goes down to the river; it drifts homeward missing its people instead. That is not a metric moving, it is a named journey disappearing from a creature's life and being replaced by a different one.

AND IT EXPLAINS EVERY OTHER WITNESS AT ONCE. If a creature never undertakes a thirst errand:
    it plans no route to water        -> 0 plan_to_room searches, 0 memo consultations
    it is never thwarted en route     -> no Frustrated, no learned Helplessness
    its thirst never escalates by heat-> hot and temperate reach distress the same day
    it never strands                  -> chronicity 0, recovery in 4 ticks
    a neighbour cannot help it        -> co-located worth exactly 0
Nine witnesses, one cause, and it is visible in a sentence a reader would read.

THE WARRANT'S TEST ANTICIPATED YOUR SITUATION AND NAMES THE FORK. Its message says two causes produce this and they take OPPOSITE remedies: (1) a provenance regression, where the stream stopped carrying what the prose carried -- DO NOT regenerate, fix; or (2) "THE WALK ITSELF MOVED -- a terrain, drive, arbitration, clock or pathfinding change made this seed's creatures do something different." Yours is unambiguously (2). It also warns that re-capturing the before-image requires building at the campaign's merge base where the per-step prose is still live, never re-deriving from current code.

SO THE QUESTION I HAVE ASKED FOR FOUR ROUNDS NOW HAS A CONCRETE FORM, and it is a world question rather than a test question: IS A WORLD WHERE A THIRSTY CREATURE NO LONGER GOES TO THE RIVER THE WORLD THIS CAMPAIGN INTENDS? If yes, that is a large, defensible design change and it wants a decision record, not six relaxed assertions -- and the six calibration witnesses are then measuring a world that no longer exists and should be retired deliberately rather than loosened. If no, the anchor is reaching past its intent and every one of those witnesses was right the first time.

Your round-4 work on The Culvert showed you can re-key a witness while keeping its floor. Three independent campaigns' guards have now caught this -- The Culvert's, turn_budget's denominator, and The Warrant's before-image -- and none of them was written with your campaign in mind. That is what a working immune system looks like; the question is only whether the thing it is rejecting is meant to be there.

Stage gate, nothing pushed, main untouched at fff169c65.
